chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah, the Exalted, support him—informed us of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, all together from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Will you not inform me from where you knew and said, ‘Indeed, the wiping is over part of the head and part of the feet’? He laughed and then said: ‘O Zurārah, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said it, and the Book from Allah, the Exalted, was revealed with it.
Because Allah, the Exalted, says: ‘So wash your faces.’
So we knew that the entire face should be washed. Then He said:
‘And your hands up to the elbows.’
Then He separated between the two statements and said:

So we knew, when He said ‘with your heads,’ that the wiping is over part of the head because of the letter bā’. Then He joined the feet to the head, just as He joined the two hands to the face, and said:
‘And your feet up to the ankles.’
So we knew, when He joined them to the head, that the wiping is over part of them. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله explained that to the people, but they neglected it. Then He said:
‘Then if you do not find water, perform tayammum with clean earth, and wipe your faces and your hands.’

So when He lifted wudu from one who does not find water, He established wiping in place of washing, because He said ‘with your faces,’ then joined to it ‘and your hands.’ Then He said ‘from it,’ meaning from that tayammum, because He knew that all of that would not pass over the face, since some of that earth adheres to part of the palm and does not adhere to another part of it. Then He said:
‘Allah does not intend to place upon you any hardship.’

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: tayammum, dry ablution with clean earth when water is unavailable
key_terms.الرَّأْسِ: the head, over part of which wiping is performed in wudu
key_terms.الرِّجْلَيْنِ: the feet, linked here to wiping in the Qur'anic reading and explanation
key_terms.الصَّعِيدِ: clean earth or ground used for tayammum
key_terms.الْحَرَجُ: hardship or constriction, negated here as a divine intent in the law
key_terms.الْكِتَابُ: the revealed Book, i.e. the Qur'an, as proof for the ruling
key_terms.الْمَسْحَ: wiping in ritual purification, as opposed to washing
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the prescribed ritual purification before salat

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Bāqir عليه السلام derive wiping part of the head and feet in wudu from the Qur'an?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the rulings of wudu and tayammum through the wording of the Qur'an as taught by Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام. It argues that the Qur'anic structure indicates washing the whole face and arms, but wiping only part of the head and feet, and it presents this as the teaching of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. It also explains that tayammum is a divinely legislated ease and that Allah does not intend hardship for the believers.
